description:
lightweight, open-source network monitor for Windows that displays live upload/download speeds directly on the Taskbar with a native look and feel.

A lightweight, open-source network monitor for Windows that displays live upload/download speeds directly on the Taskbar with a native look and feel.
✨ NetSpeedTray 2.2.1
The first patch after 2.2.0. Multi-GPU PCs get every GPU in the hover card, hybrid laptops get their NVIDIA GPU's sleep back, and the 0.5 s update rate I promised is here as an option. It also wakes far less often in the background, so it's lighter on a laptop battery.
Highlights
- Every GPU in the hover card. On a PC with two or more, each gets its own usage, temperature, power and memory. The taskbar still shows one. Thanks @balciseri.
- Better battery on Optimus laptops. NetSpeedTray no longer wakes a sleeping NVIDIA GPU just to read its temperature.
- A 0.5 s update rate, if you want it. "Real-time (0.5s)" on the Update rate slider; 1 s stays the default. Thanks @evandrosergiooliveira-cloud.
- Update offers no longer open a window on their own. NetSpeedTray now also checks while it keeps running, and shows a small notice by the widget.
- The Wi-Fi name without Location access. Thanks @XYuki-cloud.
- Choose what the right-click menu shows (Settings → General). Thanks @kamal63442 for the idea.
- Stricter in-app updates. The installer must match the release's published checksums, and a portable update checks every file it installs, not just NetSpeedTray.exe. Thanks @kamal63442.
Top fixes
- The widget goes back onto the taskbar when Windows moves it, for example when you connect over Remote Desktop. Thanks @bobbergen.
- A CPU/GPU label color you picked stays that color on an accent-colored taskbar. When the accent color makes one of your other colors too faint, Settings now says so. Thanks @Buuuush.
- The widget no longer sits on the Desktop or Links toolbars of a Windows 10-style taskbar. Thanks @Achaean.
- With a VPN up, Check connection pings your real router instead of the VPN's far end.
- Light traffic reads "<0.1 Mbps" instead of "0.0" with "Always show megabytes" on, so a quiet connection doesn't look broken. Thanks @Buuuush.
- A new update rate applies at once, instead of after the old interval runs out.
- A click no longer nudges the widget. A tiny mouse movement during a click used to count as a drag and save a new spot. Thanks @RunningDead89.
Heads up
- Update offers show as a notice above the widget. Check for Updates in the right-click menu still opens the full window, and "Not now" holds a version back for 3 days.
- On a multi-GPU PC the hover card's GPU list replaces the single GPU and VRAM rows. It's on by default; the switch is under the GPU picker in Settings → Hardware.
- On a hybrid laptop, GPU temperature and power show "—" while the NVIDIA GPU sleeps, with an "Idle" tag on the hover card.
- RAM and VRAM can now show without CPU or GPU monitoring. If you had them switched on with CPU or GPU monitoring off, the widget shows them now.
- Two renames, same settings: the 1 s update rate is Standard (1s) (it was "Aggressive"), and the update switch is Check for updates automatically.
There's more in the changelog, including line spacing between the speed rows, and Bengali digits and Bengali Monitor graphs.
Thanks
Code from @kamal63442, @XYuki-cloud and @pasharm, bug reports and testing from @balciseri, @Buuuush, @bobbergen, @Achaean, @RainThings, @bober233, @evandrosergiooliveira-cloud and @RunningDead89, and translations and reviews from @Askeleid, @cscsanaki and @coolvitto. And thanks to everyone who ran the beta.
Full changelog: https://github.com/erez-c137/NetSpeedTray/blob/main/changelog.md
